text:
ana: Heads up — trying to make the quickstart sample run on Bun and Netlify Edge. Getting different failures: Bun errors on `export * from` in our CJS build, Netlify logs `require is not defined` in their ESM worker. Any prior art for shipping a single package that works across Node/Bun/Edge?

thomas: Oof. We've historically had to ship distinct entrypoints. package.json with `type":"module"` helps ESM-first runtimes but breaks require consumers.

rachel: We do publish both `dist/index.cjs` and `dist/index.mjs`. The tricky part is the `types` field — if `types` points to `dist/index.d.ts` but that d.ts references `export =` it confuses TS when users import the ESM entry.

ana: Currently package.json looks like: `{"main":"dist/index.cjs","module":"dist/index.mjs","types":"dist/index.d.ts"}`. No exports map.

devon: Add an exports map and typesVersions. Example: "exports":{"import":"./dist/index.mjs","require":"./dist/index.cjs","./edge":"./dist/worker.mjs" }, "typesVersions": {"*": {"*": ["dist/types/*"]}}. That lets bundlers and TS resolve correctly.

wren: For Bun specifically, it respects ESM but sometimes has issues with `exports` when a subpath is used. We published a tiny `redwood-sdk/compat` entry that re-exports the ESM module without an exports map and that fixed some Bun users. Ugly but pragmatic.

ana: TS typings are the other mess. Our client has overloaded signatures: one `create<T>(prompt: string)` and another `create<T>(opts: {input: T})`. When users omit T, inference defaults to any unless `noImplicitAny` is on. Some sample code relied on that implicit any and CI types passed, but downstream apps see `any`.

rachel: Can we flip the default generic to `unknown`? `create<T = unknown>` forces users to opt-in or assert, which is better for safety.

devon: I recommend a discriminated union single signature: `create<T = unknown>(opts: {mode: 'text'|'structured'; input: string | T}): Promise<Response<T>>`. That keeps inference tighter and avoids overload ambiguity.

thomas: Also watch out for `declaration: true` + `isolatedModules: true` in tsconfig. esbuild/tsup will fail emitting d.ts if isolatedModules is required. For sample builds we often override tsconfig to `isolatedModules: false` and let rollup/tsc emit types in CI.

wren: For samples we added a minimal `tsconfig.sample.json` with `module: ESNext, target: ES2020, isolatedModules: true, declaration: false`. Keeps esbuild happy and avoids weird transforms.

ana: One more gotcha: `preserveValueImports` changed how imports are elided and broke a helper that relied on side-effect imports. Setting it off for sample builds fixed it.

ci-bot: ci: sample-build-bun (node 20) failed. netlify-edge build shows `ReferenceError: require is not defined` in logs https://ci/edge/54321

devon: I'll prototype two small fixes this week: 1) exports map + `/edge` subpath, 2) single generic signature + discriminant union for create.

rachel: Can we also add a one-file `edge-quickstart.mjs` in samples that only imports ESM APIs and demonstrates `await create()` with explicit generic? Short doc to show `import {createClient} from 'redwood-sdk/edge'` and `const res = await client.create<MyType>({mode:'structured', input: {...}})`.

ana: I'll open the PR with three commits: packaging (exports/typesVersions), typings (single generic), samples (edge/bun quickstarts + tsconfig.sample). Mark it `devex` and tag @devon @wren for runtime checks.

thomas: Nice. Also add a note in SDK README about `types` vs `typesVersions` for multi-target packages — it's saved a lot of headaches.

wren: Tiny follow-up: add a test matrix for Bun/Node/Netlify Edge to CI (can be opt-in slow job) to prevent regressions.

ana: Will do. Thanks all — huge improvement for onboarding if we get this right.
